_why: The board for 'which scheduled job has stopped producing'. The first widget
is the ZERO-WRITE MONITOR'S OWN QUERY, by job instead of per job, so the
board and the alarm cannot disagree: dashboards-agreement.test.ts renders
monitor-zero-write.json through apply-monitors.sh and compares the two
clamp_max skeletons, rather than restating the formula here.
title: UseMoney — job health
description: managed-by:apply-dashboards — edit the file, not the UI

definition.title: Selected but wrote nothing (36h) — the monitor's own query
definition._why: clamp_max(selected,1) - clamp_max(written,1) > 0 is the truth table: found work and produced nothing ALERTS, a partial write does not, and genuinely idle (0/0) does not. A bare ratio or subtraction loses all three distinctions.

definition.title: Rows selected by job
definition._why: Selected WITHOUT written is the half that makes a zero honest: a job that selects nothing is idle, a job that selects and writes nothing is broken, and the two are byte-identical if you only plot writes.

definition.title: Upstream (transport) failures by job
definition._why: Its own counter because it is not measured in ROWS — a 403 from an upstream is a reason no rows were considered, and folding it into `failed` is what hid Tickertape's egress block for five months.

definition.title: Rows that failed to persist, by job
EDGAR detection latency p95 (s)
definition._why: A DogStatsD histogram, so the sidecar aggregates it into .avg/.count/.max/.median/.95percentile sub-series — the base name `stockbook.edgar.detect_latency_seconds` carries no points of its own and a widget on it renders empty.
